title: Workplace injury compensation - the employer's liability explained
p1:
A workplace accident can happen in seconds. But who carries the responsibility after it happens?

Many people assume an injury at work is simply the employee's problem. That belief can lead to costly mistakes.
p2:
The surprising truth: an employer may have a legal responsibility to compensate an injured worker, even when the accident was not intentional.

Workplace injury compensation is not just about fault. It is often about whether the employer provided a safe working environment and followed required safety measures.
p3:
In simple terms, employers have a duty to reduce workplace risks. If an employee is injured while performing their job, compensation may cover losses such as medical expenses, lost wages, or rehabilitation costs depending on the applicable law.

A safe workplace protects both employees and businesses. Knowing these responsibilities can help workers understand their rights and help employers prevent avoidable risks.
conclusion: Do you think most employees know what compensation they may be entitled to after a workplace injury?
